newsitem.title: POLAND: Warta eyes foreign investor by mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Warta eyes foreign investor by mid-1997.

text.p: Polish insurance firm TUiR Warta SA hopes to find a foreign investor who would take about 20-percent stake in the company by mid-1997, the company's president said on Monday.

"We are holding talks with potential candidates, mainly from the insurance sector and we hope we would be able to finalize it this year ... we would like (to find an investor) by mid-1997," Andrzej Witkowski told a news conference.
Earlier Warta has signalled it would carry out a new share issue for the foreign investor.
Currently Warta has 3.46 million shares outstanding and its main stockholders are the state treasury, with a 34.7 percent stake and Elektrim with 10.1 percent.
But it plans to issue in February between 865,380 to 2,596,139 shares to Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Kredyt Bank, state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) and two current shareholders.
